kind: Deployment-variant screen (memory-feasible execution change); decided before any comparison-run evaluation was scored
question: Does adamw_bnb_8bit at the native per-rank 128-sample microbatch (128 x grad_accum 2, global batch 2048), which FusedAdam cannot run with checkpoints on 8x A100-80GB, train at least ~5% faster than FusedAdam's best feasible setting (64 x grad_accum 4)?

measurement.method: steady-state seconds per iteration from native iter_speed receipts; excludes each process's first iteration and checkpoint-save iterations (> 60 s)

decision: Speedup is ~0%, far below the ~5% screen. The deployment-variant arm is NOT added; no addendum arm, no extra runs. The primary like-for-like protocol is unchanged.
mechanism: Step time is compute-bound and independent of microbatch size at a fixed 2048 global batch (the same ~46 s/iter at 64 x 4 and 128 x 2), so the eight-bit memory saving does not translate into a faster execution configuration on this node. The feasibility difference itself is retained as a reported result: at 128 x 2 eight-bit trains and publishes checkpoints (peak 80.1 GiB) where FusedAdam fails its first checkpoint save (peak 81.2 GiB).
evaluation_harness_note: Closed-loop evaluation runs the native action_policy_server_libero with --no-guardrails (new eval-only opt-in; default remains on). Guardrails screen free-form prompts/frames and never alter generated actions; LIBERO-10 prompts are the fixed benchmark task strings. The default path needs the optional better_profanity package and guardrail weights that the offline evaluation environment does not carry (eval smoke 38695975 failed on that import). Applied identically to every evaluated checkpoint of both arms.

activation_checkpointing_probe.hypothesis: Native selective AC (save attention, recompute the rest) spends recompute; the ~5.2 GiB/rank 8-bit saving could pay for lighter AC and reduce compute, giving a setting 8-bit fits within 80 GiB (including checkpoint save) that FusedAdam does not, >=5% faster than FusedAdam 64x4.

activation_checkpointing_probe.decision: No lighter AC policy fits for either optimizer at 64x4; the 8-bit saving (~5.2 GiB/rank) is smaller than the extra activation memory of either relaxation. No 8-bit-exclusive faster setting exists. No addendum; the speed route is closed. The locked protocol and runs are unchanged.
activation_checkpointing_probe.not_pursued: Smaller microbatches with relaxed AC shrink activations for both arms alike, so they cannot create an 8-bit-exclusive setting except by coincidence at the margin; not run (finite probe as directed).
